claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is metastable and single-phase, likely with a near-BCC structure.
The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a random elemental distribution with no significant chemical short-range order.
Annealing at 800–1000 K can promote nanoscale chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr without causing coarse grain growth or loss of the single-phase state.
The annealing treatment will produce Hf–Ti- or Ti–Zr-enriched short-range-ordered regions.
Chemical short-range order reinforces local bonding in HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical short-range order reduces local lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Nanoscale short-range-ordered clusters enhance load transfer.
Nanoscale short-range-ordered clusters provide vibrational clamping.
Reducing atomic-scale lattice fluctuations through short-range order stiffens local regions.
The annealed, short-range-ordered alloy will have a higher elevated-temperature elastic modulus than the as-cast alloy.
Short-range order will modify yield behavior and may increase yield strength relative to the as-cast alloy.
Short-range order will alter the strain-hardening response relative to the as-cast alloy.
Short-range order restricts atomic vibrations in HfNbTaTiZr.
The annealed, short-range-ordered alloy will have a lower coefficient of thermal expansion than the disordered as-cast alloy.
The predicted short-range-order effects should hold from 300 K to 1200 K.
Below 300 K, quantum or other low-temperature mechanisms may dominate the measured responses.
Above 1200 K, grain coarsening and diffusion-induced creep may mask the effects of short-range order.
